I've shortened the scroll-switching wait in the spec; the code isn't changed yet. `piton check` finds no problems, formatting is clean, and `piton build` succeeded.

**Why it feels long:** the code waits for the wheel to be still for 250 ms before counting a scroll as new. During the 450 ms slide, every wheel event also restarts that wait. So if you keep scrolling while it slides, crossing back can take close to 700 ms or more.

**What I changed:** two edits to `MessageListScrollingShape.scrollingPast` in `spec/scope/prompt-mode/message-list/Scrolling.pi`:

- **The pause is now fixed and short.** The wheel or trackpad being still for 80 ms makes the next scroll new, and lifting your fingers off the trackpad and putting them back counts as new straight away. - **Scrolling during the slide no longer adds to the wait.** Once the slide settles, the same 80 ms pause is all that's needed, counted from your last scroll whether it came during the slide or after. The wheel still scrolls neither view while the slide runs, and a scroll carried on in the same motion still never crosses over.

I left the slide's own length alone, since it's the wait you said is too long, not the animation. If the slide also feels slow once the pause is fixed, shortening it is a separate change.

- **`MessageListScrollingShape.scrollingPast`**, as above.

  - In `scroll_past_ends`, the check that a slide is still running blocks the wheel; that part stays.
  - The rule that a trackpad touch starting (`TouchPhase::Started`) counts as a new scroll stays.
  - The test `scrolling_past_an_end_crosses_over` sleeps `PANE_SLIDE_TIME + SCROLL_REST` and should still hold.

content.text:
The pause before a scroll switches views is now 80 ms instead of 250 ms. I haven't tried it in the app, so I can't say yet whether it feels immediate enough.

The fix was a single constant, `SCROLL_REST` in `src/prompt_mode.rs`. The rest of the spec's new wording already matched the code:
- **A new trackpad touch** counts as a new scroll straight away, with no pause.
- **During the slide,** the wheel still scrolls neither view and can't cross back. Your last scroll during the slide still counts, so once the slide settles, 80 ms of stillness after that scroll is all that's needed. Scrolling during the slide no longer stretches the wait much, because the pause itself is now so short.
- **No other delays:** nothing extra is waited for after reaching an end, or before the switch.

The slide itself still takes 450 ms. If it's the animation that feels slow now, shortening it is a separate change.

**Tests:** the build has no warnings, and `scrolling_past_an_end_crosses_over` still passes. The full suite has the same 7 failures as last time:
- **Four were already failing before these changes:** the three prompt-wording tests in `hidden_anchor.rs` and `system_prompts.rs`, and `code_tasks_sent_to_spec_are_told_what_the_code_task_did`.
- **Three passed when I ran each on its own last time:** `batch_sent_tasks_run_in_order_in_the_other_mode`, `selected_answer_text_can_be_copied_or_attached` and `raw_prompt_opens_once_the_task_has_compiled`. I didn't rerun them individually this time.

The spec and your prompt didn't disagree. The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1790709326-Prompt_d21629ee1cca281c.understanding.md`.
